intro.title: Micro-frontends
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web application that demonstrates the core idea of micro-frontends by combining two independent frontend modules into a single page. You will learn how micro-frontends allow different parts of a web app to be developed, deployed, and updated separately. The main technologies you'll use are JavaScript modules and basic DOM manipulation to load and display these modules. By the end, you'll understand how this approach improves team scalability and maintainability in frontend development.
intro.usecase: Micro-frontends are used in large-scale web applications where independent teams need to develop, deploy, and scale features autonomously. For example, an e-commerce platform like Amazon might use micro-frontends for distinct sections such as the product recommendation panel, the shopping cart module, and the checkout form—each built and updated separately. This pattern is also common in enterprise dashboards, where different teams own widgets like analytics charts, user management tables, or notification feeds, enabling faster iteration without full-page redeploys. As a frontend developer, you might implement micro-frontends to integrate a third-party payment gateway or a legacy application into a modern React shell, ensuring modularity and team independence.
